name: Wamas
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Z'graggen 1980 comparative wordlists located; no grammar/phonology of Wamas found

sources.citation: SIL PNG Language Resources: Wamas [wmc] (www-01.sil.org/pacific/png, the Internet Archive 2015; pnglanguages.sil.org current page could not be reached by automated download).
sources.note: 'Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' No SIL survey, phonology or dictionary listed.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3, p. 7 (applies to all languages in the study): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Wamas entry 2.21.12.18 gives villages and a note on Kasprus only; Mabuso typology sec. 2.21.16 is segmental/morphological only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: Same stress-omitted sentence (pp. 13-14); Wamas entry 2.21.12.18: 'I had no opportunity to collect materials' (classification then based on Kasprus's 'Ate' list, later re-identified as Murupi).
Zero grammar/phonology/sketch references; only Z'graggen overviews/wordlist, Ethnologue, ELCat.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Wamas language [wmc] (language-archives.org, Internet Archive copy 2025).
sources.note: Lists only Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List entries; no description.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (Wamas = language C12)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction sec. 6 (pp. viii-ix) says transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and lists fluctuating sounds per language (Wamas: d~r, j~z~dz~y~d); no stress marks in the lists and no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
sources.note: Gazetteer/map volume; no stress content (a full-text search for stress/accent empty).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Wamas appears only in classification lists and comparative tables.
Lexical data only, all from Z'graggen 1980; no suprasegmental information.

sources.citation: Kasprus, Aloys. 1942-45. Die Sprachen des Mugilgebietes, NO-Neuguinea. Anthropos 37-40: 711-778 (Hanseman wordlists incl. 'Ate', pp. 742-767).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other primary lexical source for the Hanseman area; German missionary wordlists sometimes mark accent. Caveat: Z'graggen 1971:2.21.12.18 says Kasprus's 'Ate' list corresponds to Murupi, not Wamas, so relevance to wama1247 is doubtful.

sources.citation: Any unpublished SIL-PNG sociolinguistic survey or organised phonology data covering the Hanseman languages west of Madang (Wamas/Samosa/Murupi/Mosimo cluster), SIL Ukarumpa archives.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL PNG public catalogue lists nothing for wmc (2015 and current), but unprocessed survey wordlists with stress marks may exist in the Ukarumpa archive; would be the only route to a first-hand stress observation.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. (collector, compiler). n.d. [1960s-70s fieldwork]. Wamas (Madang Comparative Wordlists). Field notebook, Museum der Kulturen Basel Vb-34838.0840; PARADISEC collection JZ3, item JZ3-WAMAS (57 page scan, JPEG/TIFF). DOI 10.26278/GENT-BG28.
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Catalogue record only. A handwritten comparative wordlist notebook (c. 300 items); the published version (D-32) is 'semi-phonemic' with no suprasegmental marks, but field notebooks of this series sometimes carry stress/pitch diacritics that were dropped in publication. No tone analysis expected; at most raw prosodic marks.
